idiom_name: no sealed types at runtime: frozen tagged objects + a checked union layer
implementation_notes: Plain JavaScript has no closed-type facility, so the closest runtime approximation is a family of factory functions returning `Object.freeze`d tagged objects (`{ kind: 'card', number }`), consumed by a `switch` on `kind` whose `default` throws: the freeze stops property changes (silently in sloppy mode, `TypeError` in strict mode/ESM) but nothing prevents a new `kind` from appearing, and no construct checks exhaustiveness. The closure therefore has a real home only in a type layer - TypeScript discriminated unions with a `never`-guarded default, available to plain `.js` through `// @ts-check` and JSDoc `@typedef` unions - plus boundary validation for data that did not originate inside the program. Use the frozen-object convention only for genuinely closed internal vocabularies; for extension points use plain classes or functions and document the contract.
pitfalls: `Object.freeze` is shallow: nested objects and arrays stay mutable, so a frozen case can still change through its fields.
Freezing fails silently in sloppy-mode code (assignment without error), so the mutation bug is invisible unless the code runs in strict mode/ESM.
A missing `default` in a JS `switch` silently returns `undefined`, and the `never`-typed guard exists only where a checker runs - never at runtime.

Discriminant widening: a `kind` built from a plain string variable is inferred as `string`, which kills narrowing for every later switch - keep the literal inline, freeze the object literal, or use `as const` in the TS layer.
alternative: Move the union into a checked type layer: TypeScript discriminated unions with `readonly` fields and a `never`-guarded default arm (usable from plain JavaScript via `// @ts-check` and JSDoc `@typedef` unions), validated at the boundary by a runtime schema validator so unverified data never enters the union.
